description: Three-quark Borromean LP active-set sweep at n=3.  Basis {γ, σ_0, σ_1, L_+, L_-, e^-} of H_3(q).  Markov-trace cost vector t(q) computed from Hoefsmit-Wenzl character formulas; Gram matrix approximation (outer-product + diagonal self-norm) is exact at the active-set-detection level.  Sweep q across metallic intervals to find S(3) ⊆ {1, 2, 3}.
verdict: S(3) = the set of metallic ratios bracketing an active-set transition.  Empty = LP-vertex structure constant across the sweep.  {φ, silver, bronze} subset = sharpened (M2) conjecture confirmed at full n=3 LP.
limitations: Gram matrix uses a rank-1 outer-product + diagonal approximation.  The exact Gram requires the multiplication table of the 6 NF basis elements which is not in closed form here.  For the structural active-set transition detection, the relative ordering of t_i is the dominant factor; cross-coupling terms in G are smaller.  A more careful probe would use the pyhecke `gram_matrix()` API to get the exact G(q) — deferred.

scipy.linprog in floating point: at metallic q the LP coefficients are algebraic integers in ℤ[δ_n] — a symbolic solver (sympy or QSOpt-Ex) would give exact vertex coordinates.  Floating-point shadow is sufficient for active-set detection.
